status: USER-REPORTED fixed-tic hardware results; one run per variant
transcription: Revision, count, completion, mean frame time, zero decode rows, final tic and sequence hash read from the original photographs and enlarged crops. This record deliberately omits min/max and present-call timings.
interpretation: Both variants completed 30 measured frames at tic 40 with the expected EBC8D404 image sequence. The D00E stop is intentional.
V48 reduced mean frame time from 215 to 145 ms: 32.56% shorter, about 1.48 times the reciprocal mean rate.

Both versions share the raw pack, two frame buffers, palette snapshots, 16-column conversion, engine archive and clock settings. The bridge selects serial or overlapped presentation; all 12 other native objects are byte-identical.
This result supports cooperative rendering/presentation overlap for the fixed start-room workload; it does not isolate CPU rendering, preparation, memory copying or transfer time.
The reciprocal mean rates of 4.65 and 6.90 frames/s describe this fixed-tic benchmark, not measured normal-play FPS or input-to-display latency.
V46 timing used different diagnostic/hash placement and display batching. Do not interpret V46 to V47 as an isolated regression or V46 to V48 as an isolated overlap gain.
The 16-column path booted and completed this hardware workload. One run per variant does not establish normal-play controls, movement-scene performance or long-term stability.
Retain the V48 overlap design for subsequent development; keep V47 as its controlled benchmark reference.
